description: Machine coordination outside Team authority and durable memory behavior.

evals.name: coordinates-project-through-team
evals.prompt: Implement a multi-step feature in workspace ws_project. Coordinate it through the correct Team and explain your authority.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent explicitly selects or creates a Team, delegates to that Team's own Orchestrator, and refuses Team execution authority.
expectations: Identifies itself as the machine-level General Agent outside Team hierarchy
Contains `codeterm team list` before Team creation or delegation
Contains either `codeterm agent spawn ... --role Orchestrator --workspace ws_project --task ...` for a missing Team or `codeterm send ... --tab ...` to delegate to an existing Team Orchestrator
Does NOT claim to be a Team Orchestrator, own the Team plan, dispatch plan tasks, or judge Team work

evals.name: retains-machine-control
evals.prompt: This is only a capability question; do not execute anything. Tell me whether you can coordinate workspaces and Teams, control agents, contact a mesh peer, schedule cron, use the Telegram bridge, and recall/save/graph memory. State every Team-plan action you cannot perform.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent explicitly retains workspace, Team, agent, mesh, cron, bridge, and memory control while refusing Team plan execution.
expectations: The explanation explicitly states control of workspaces, Team creation or selection, and agent spawn or control
The explanation explicitly states control of mesh, cron, bridges, and persistent memory recall/save/graph
The explanation explicitly denies Team plan ownership, approval, dispatch, judging, and mutation authority

evals.name: memory-recall-save-and-graph
evals.prompt: This is an explicit remember instruction; do not ask for approval. Tell me what you remember about Alex and immediately remember that Alex now works on Project Cedar, starting today. No memory command has returned an id yet. Show only the safe commands before those results exist and state that you will inspect them and search again for any missing endpoint id.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent searches, saves immediately in English, and stops before graph mutation until real endpoint ids are returned.
expectations: First uses `codeterm mem search --json` in English before answering about Alex
Then immediately uses `codeterm mem save --json --kind fact` with an English title and body
Does NOT emit `codeterm mem graph relate` while actual endpoint ids are unavailable
Explains that it will inspect returned ids and search again for any missing endpoint before graph mutation
Distinguishes durable facts from past sessions and folder skills

evals.name: memory-temporal-edge-uses-returned-ids
evals.prompt: The completed memory commands returned person_7 as Alex's id and project_9 as Project Cedar's id. Record that Alex works on Project Cedar starting 2026-08-02. Use those exact returned ids.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent creates the temporal relationship with the exact returned ids and canonical graph syntax.
expectations: Uses `codeterm mem graph relate --from person_7 --rel works_on --to project_9 --valid-from 2026-08-02`

evals.name: recovers-child-startup-prompt
evals.prompt: You spawned a Team Orchestrator in tab child_7 with an assigned task. The tab remains Waiting. Its visible numbered provider picker already selects option 1, Yes. `codeterm tab respond 1 --tab child_7` returned success, but a second inspection shows the exact same picker. Explain the next bounded recovery commands.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent verifies the exact child screen, presses only Enter for the already-selected visible option, then verifies that the agent resumed without resending its task.
expectations: Rechecks the exact tab with `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_7` before the fallback
Uses exactly one bounded `codeterm send --tab child_7 --actions "enter"` fallback because the desired visible option is already selected
Uses `codeterm tab status --tab child_7` afterward to verify the child resumed
Does not resend the assigned task payload or guess provider-specific keys

evals.name: holds-inspected-slow-startup
evals.prompt: A CodeTerm startup report says child_9 has not acknowledged attempt pty_9 after 30 seconds and will close at 60 seconds. `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_9` shows the provider is legitimately still initializing, with no picker or failure. Explain the bounded action. Do not use a delay.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent preserves only the inspected startup attempt with startup-hold and waits for pushed evidence rather than sleeping or inventing readiness.
expectations: Uses `codeterm agent startup-hold --tab child_9 --attempt pty_9`
Does not use sleep, delayed polling, screen-text readiness heuristics, or resend the assigned task
Does not run `codeterm agent startup-ack` on the child's behalf; the bounded parent action is only `startup-hold`

evals.name: recovers-exited-provider-in-place
evals.prompt: `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_4` confirms `backing.kind=pty` and a verified Claude session. `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_4` shows a shell prompt after the provider exited. The user wants that same conversation back in that tab. Explain the commands.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent recovers the exited provider in place with agent restart, verifies liveness afterward, and falls back to a fresh spawn only when that restart refuses.
expectations: Uses `codeterm agent restart --tab child_4` as the recovery command
Does NOT spawn a new agent or open a new tab before trying that restart, and does NOT use `--force`
Uses the verified session evidence from `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_4` and the visible screen from `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_4`
After the `codeterm agent restart --tab child_4` command, checks that child_4 is live (for example with `codeterm tab list`)
Checks `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_4` or `codeterm tab status --tab child_4` after restart
Names spawning a fresh agent only as the fallback for when that restart refuses (no verified session, or no owning provider)

evals.name: changes-visible-model-picker-one-step-at-a-time
evals.prompt: The assigned route explicitly authorizes choosing Model B for child_10. `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_10` confirms a PTY and the child's bound provider session. The visible model picker has Model A selected and Model B immediately below it; this is a navigable list, not a numbered provider prompt. Give the exact bounded commands and verification order.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent reads the current picker, moves down once, rereads to confirm Model B is selected, presses Enter once, then rereads and verifies the model and session remain correct.
expectations: Uses `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_10` before acting
Moves one visible step with `codeterm send --tab child_10 --actions "down"` and rereads before Enter
Presses Enter only after confirming Model B is selected, then rereads the screen
Checks `codeterm tab status --tab child_10` afterward for session and acknowledgement state
Changes the model only because the route explicitly authorizes Model B

evals.name: repairs-authorized-shell-command-from-visible-error
evals.prompt: The route explicitly authorizes running `git status --short` in child_11. `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_11` confirms `backing.kind=pty` and no live agent session owns the shell input. `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_11` shows the attempted command `git status --shrot`, its unknown-option error, and a new PowerShell prompt. Explain how to correct and verify this command without inspecting another surface.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent uses the authorized command and visible typo as evidence, sends only `git status --short` to that shell with Enter, then rereads the same tab to verify the result.
expectations: Confirms the exact target is a PTY shell with `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_11`
Confirms there is no live agent session owning the shell input
Uses only the route-authorized `git status --short` command and does not invent another shell command
Sends the command as PTY text with Enter and rereads `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_11` afterward
Does not use external UI automation

evals.name: escalates-unknown-interactive-screen-without-keys
evals.prompt: Startup acknowledgement is missing for child_12. `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_12` confirms a PTY, but `codeterm tab get-text --tab child_12` shows an unfamiliar full-screen prompt with no readable title, option labels, or selected item. Explain what you do next.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent preserves the tab and escalates with the observed state, without sending text or keys based on a guess.
expectations: Does not use `tab respond`, `send --actions`, or a shell command on child_12
Escalates the ambiguous screen to the responsible owner with the observed state
Does not restart, rebind, or repair the tab without evidence

evals.name: never-runs-shell-command-in-chat-backend
evals.prompt: An assigned child named child_13 has not acknowledged startup. `codeterm tab inspect --tab child_13` shows `backing.kind=chat_backend`; there is no terminal screen or shell. The route allows asking the child whether it is ready. Explain the safe contact and recovery boundary.
evals.expected_output: The General Agent uses chat text if needed, reports that the child has no shell, and never gives it a shell command or terminal key sequence.
expectations: Identifies `backing.kind=chat_backend` as having no shell
Uses chat text only for the authorized contact
Does NOT send a shell command, `tab exec` request, or `send --actions` sequence to child_13
Does not claim that a chat response is the PTY startup acknowledgement
